purpose: Replace every genuinely ternary OR clause by a constant-size topology-changing gadget using only two bijunctive clauses and one affine XOR3 equation. This creates an exact alternative frontier in which each local constraint family is polynomial by itself (2-SAT/SCC and XOR-SAT/Gaussian elimination) and all hardness is isolated in their coupling.

single_clause_gadget.input_clause: C=(a OR b OR c), where a,b,c are arbitrary Boolean literals.
constraints: y_C XOR b XOR z_C = 1, where b denotes the truth value of literal b
single_clause_gadget.identity: (a OR b OR c) iff exists y_C,z_C satisfying the three gadget constraints.

proof.unsatisfied_input: If a=b=c=0, the first binary clause forces y=0 and the last binary clause forces z=0, contradicting y XOR b XOR z=1.
satisfied_input: If b=1, choose y=z (for example y=z=0); the XOR equation holds, and the two binary clauses can be satisfied because at least one of a,b,c is true.
More generally the exact checker exhausts all eight values of (a,b,c) and both auxiliary bits and verifies that the projected gadget relation is precisely OR3.
proof.projection: Because y_C,z_C are private to clause C, existential projection commutes across clauses. Replacing every 3-clause independently therefore preserves satisfiability exactly.

global_normal_form.output: B(F) AND A(F), where B(F) is a 2-CNF and A(F) is a system of arity-three affine equations over GF(2).
global_normal_form.size: Two fresh variables, two binary clauses, and one XOR3 equation per original 3-clause; construction size is linear.
global_normal_form.affine_sparsity: Every XOR row contains exactly two private auxiliary variables y_C,z_C and one original literal value b. Hence the rows are linearly independent through their private y_C columns and Gaussian elimination alone cannot couple different clauses.
global_normal_form.witness_reconstruction: A satisfying assignment of the gadget formula restricts to a satisfying assignment of F. Conversely, for a satisfying assignment of F, each clause's private y_C,z_C can be chosen independently by a constant-size truth-table lookup.

theorem.name: ARBITRARY_3SAT_HAS_AN_EXACT_BIJUNCTIVE_PLUS_AFFINE_NORMAL_FORM
theorem.statement: There is a linear-time many-one reduction from arbitrary 3-SAT to satisfiability of a conjunction of 2-CNF clauses and XOR3 equations, with linear witness reconstruction in both directions.
theorem.meaning: SCC and Gaussian elimination are individually complete for their own layers, but merely possessing both polynomial solvers does not solve their coupled satisfiability problem. The coupling itself carries arbitrary 3-SAT.

positive: A new topology-changing algebraic carrier replaces non-affine OR3 nodes by parity-friendly XOR3 nodes plus only binary gates.
The remaining frontier can be phrased as exact interaction between a bijunctive implication graph and a sparse affine system.
anti_loop: Do not claim that alternating SCC closure and Gaussian elimination is complete without a new interaction theorem; this normal form already represents arbitrary 3-SAT.
Do not count separate polynomial solvability of the two layers as progress toward the coupled problem.
not_killed: A nontrivial joint elimination theorem exploiting the very special private-auxiliary XOR rows.
A holographic/Pfaffian transformation of the topology-changed EQ/OR2/XOR3 network.

next_target.name: E8_OR2_XOR3_TOPOLOGY_CHANGED_MATCHGATE_TEST_V4_2
next_target.directive: Test whether the exact OR2+XOR3 gadget vocabulary, together with equality fanout, admits a determinant/Pfaffian realization unavailable to the original EQ3+OR3 network. First test common-basis parity exactly; if that fails, move only to genuinely edge-dependent/nonlocal gauges.

sources: T. J. Schaefer, The Complexity of Satisfiability Problems, STOC 1978, 216-226.
